where ἑβδόμαις [on the seventh], which Thomas Magister took as said for ἑπτά [seven], if it were read correctly, would have to be understood of the seventh of the gates, where the leaders cast lots as to which of the seven gates each should have to defend, as Valckenaer noted in his Diatribe on Aristobulus p. 119. But since a noun is needed to be joined with the adjective ἀγήνορες [manly], the conjecture of Heimsoeth (Krit. Studien 1 p. 301) is more probable: ἑπτὰ δ᾽ ἀγάνορες μέδοντες στρατού | δορυσόῳ σαγᾷ πρέποντος πύλαις προσίστανται πάλῳ λαχόντες [seven manly leaders of the army, conspicuous in their spear-shaking armor, take their stand at the gates, having obtained them by lot].
